title: fix(fields): store a typed percent within the ruled `scale + 2` fraction width (objectui#9810)
body:
Fixes #9810

Clause-②: no

The accept set of this package does not move outward: no new key, no new published
symbol, no new declaration read. `storedFraction` is module-private and is not
re-exported through the barrel (the same shape `percent-scale.ts` and
`numberBadInput.tsx` already use in this package), so the published surface of
`@object-ui/fields` is byte-identical. What changes is the VALUE this widget hands
to its host's `onChange` for a fraction-stored percent — a runtime emission, and it
moves toward the declared contract rather than away from it.

## The ruling this implements

Maintainer ruling, batch #161 item 3, letter B (comment 5729749935), maintainer
「其他同意」 2026-09-18T12:07Z, director seat summon #24. Operative clause, quoted:

> `scale` on a `percent` field means the DISPLAYED percentage-point decimals — the
> landed objectui#9295 convention; the storage side derives: for a fraction-stored
> percent (`percentScaleOf` = `fraction`) the objectql record validator's
> `max_scale` branch allows `scale + 2` decimal places in the stored fraction; the
> spec docblock states both; ⛔ no second member

The DISPLAY half of that clause is already landed in this repository and is left
exactly where it was: objectui#9295 on the read-only cell, the grid summary footer
and the record summary chip, objectui#9568 (PR objectui#9804) on this widget, and
objectui#9808 (PR objectui#9919) on the out-of-range width both faces take. This
branch re-derived all of it by symbol on today's `origin/main` and moved none of it.

What was NOT landed is this widget's ability to MEET the derivation.

## The defect — our own arithmetic, not the author's value

`PercentField` converted a typed percentage-point value to its stored fraction with
`n / 100`. Division by 100 is not representable in binary floating point, so the
quotient carried residue nobody typed. Measured over the whole step grid a
`scale: 2` percent field offers (`0.00` through `100.00`, 10001 values), 2760 of
them — 27.6% — convert to a stored fraction of 16 to 19 decimal places:

| typed (the step this widget offers) | stored before | decimal places | stored now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `66.67` | `0.6667000000000001` | 16 | `0.6667` |
| `99.99` | `0.9998999999999999` | 16 | `0.9999` |
| `29.97` | `0.29969999999999997` | 17 | `0.2997` |
| `8.35` | `0.08349999999999999` | 17 | `0.0835` |
| `0.07` | `0.0007000000000000001` | 19 | `0.0007` |

Those counts are the reading the platform's own instrument takes: the objectql
record validator's `max_scale` branch counts decimal places off the value's
`String()` form (its `decimalPlacesOf` helper), exponent folded in, and **refuses**
a caller value exceeding the declared width — it never rounds (that repository's
2026-08-11 ruling, restated in the branch's own comment). So each row above is a
write this widget's own `step` attribute offers and the write path then refuses,
against ANY declared width — which is the affordance objectui#9810 was filed about,
surviving on the limb the ruling settled in this widget's favour.

## What moved

`fromDisplay`'s fraction arm now shifts the DECIMAL exponent two places instead of
dividing: the result is the double nearest the decimal value the author typed, so a
display value carrying `d` decimal places stores `d + 2` and no more. The `whole`
arm (a field declaring `max > 1`) keeps its identity conversion — there the typed
number IS the stored number, so there is no arithmetic of ours to correct, and the
ruling derives `scale`, not `scale + 2`, for that storage scale.

⛔ **It is not a rounding, and that boundary is pinned in both directions.** An
author who types finer than the declared width (`12.345` into a `scale: 2` field)
still stores every digit they typed and is still refused upstream. That is the ruled
behaviour: a widget-side rounding would convert the platform's refusal into the
silent data alteration the platform explicitly ruled out.

## Tests

`packages/fields/src/__tests__/PercentField.storedScale-9810.test.tsx` — 7 rows, all
driven through the rendered control (the box the author types into, and the slider),
because the emission is what the defect is about:

- the residue table above, each row asserted as the exact double AND within the
  ruled `scale + 2 = 4` places;
- a sweep of the whole `scale: 2` grid at every third step, whose offender list must
  be empty — the invariant is re-derived on every value it enumerates, not sampled
  from a remembered list;
- MUST-NOT-CHANGE control: a value the old division already got right is
  byte-identical (`12.34` ⇒ `0.1234`, `50` ⇒ `0.5`, `100` ⇒ `1`);
- MUST-NOT-CHANGE control: the `whole` convention (`max > 1`) is untouched;
- the no-rounding pin (`12.345` ⇒ `0.12345`, five places, still refused upstream);
- `scale: 0`, and the slider path sharing the one conversion.

### Reverse verification — the ablation, with on-disk proof

Run from the committed fix, through `ablation-replace.mjs` (the sibling repository's
tool, which proves the mutation landed by anchor count and blob hash rather than by
an exit code), restoring `git checkout HEAD -- path`:

```
ablation-replace: ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 9cbb65b69f93 -> 76170b9ff3dc
  fromDisplay reverted to `n / 100`
  vitest: Tests  3 failed | 4 passed (7)
    x stores an ordinary two-decimal percentage point as the value it is
      -> expected 0.6667000000000001 to be 0.6667
    x holds for every display value the declared step offers
      -> expected [ ...(936) ] to deeply equal []       (936 offenders of 3334 enumerated)
    x emits the same exact fraction from the slider as from the input
ablation-replace: ok restored: blob == HEAD (9cbb65b69f93) and `git diff HEAD` is empty
```

⭐ The direction is the ordinary one (red), and the SPLIT is the load-bearing part:
the three rows that assert the repair go red, the four control rows stay green — a
pin that also went red on its controls would be pinning the mutation, not the fix.

## Acceptance notes

**① The PM's mechanism assumption is FALSIFIED, and the card's own headline reading
is now a stale address.** The dispatch's reading — the percent edit widget reads
`precision ?? 2` while the cell reads `scale ?? 0`, so a field declaring neither
renders two widths — does not hold on today's `origin/main`. PR objectui#9804 landed
that member swap on 2026-09-18T14:58Z and PR objectui#9919 landed the width clamp at
19:42Z, both AFTER the readings on this card were taken. Re-derived by symbol, not by
line: this widget resolves ONE width, from `scale`, guarded with `typeof` so
`scale: 0` survives. The card's filer declared its readings unverified; on the
`precision`-versus-`scale` limb they were correct WHEN TAKEN and are now historical.

**② The one divergence that remains is another card's, and it is in the decision
box.** With nothing declared, this widget still keeps its own `2` while
`PercentCellRenderer` spells the same absence `0`. That is objectui#9843, which is
open, asks the maintainer for a letter (its option A declares a default in
`@objectstack/spec`; option B changes this widget), and is therefore ⛔ not touched
here and ⛔ not referenced with any keyword that would close it. Its subject is the
DEFAULT when nothing is declared; this branch only changes what happens to a value
that HAS been typed, so the two do not overlap in either direction.

**③ The upstream half of the ruling is an objectstack change, to FILE and ⛔ never to
patch from here or to compensate for on the consumer side.** Re-derived at source on
the sibling checkout's `origin/main` (commit `4efb988`): `percentScaleOf` in
`packages/spec` resolves `fraction` unless `max > 1` and its docblock states nothing
about `scale`; the objectql record validator's `max_scale` branch compares
`decimalPlacesOf(n)` against `def.scale` with NO percent arm. So the ruled
`scale + 2` allowance is not live yet — the spec docblock clause and the validator
branch plus its per-storage-scale pins are still owed there, which the ruling's own
Execution section assigns to the spec seat's vertical dispatch. Filing class **(b)**,
a declared contract not matched by the implementation. Dedupe words for whoever
files it: `max_scale percent fraction scale+2` · `record-validator percent branch
derived storage scale` · `FieldSchema scale docblock percent displayed`.
⚠️ This branch does NOT depend on that landing: today the residue values are refused
by `max_scale` for the same reason, only sooner, so the repair is correct before and
after it.

**④ Noted, ⛔ not filed.** `dataset-format.ts` in `@object-ui/core` describes this
widget in a comment as one that "divides input by 100". The sentence stays true as a
statement about MAGNITUDE (that is still the conversion), only not about the
operation, and it is outside this card's file surface. Successor who will meet it:
whoever next edits that formatter's percent path — ⛔ no PR is pending on it today.

**⑤ Scope held.** `packages/types/src/` was excluded by the dispatch (objectui#8345
and objectui#9511 are in flight there) and was not touched: `scale` is already a
declared member of `PercentFieldMetadata` (objectui#9784), so nothing was owed there.
The one file outside the declared `packages/fields/src/` surface is the changeset,
which this repo's `changeset-presence` gate mechanically requires — its lit-control
exit 1 above is the evidence it was owed.

**⑥ The orphan branch was ⛔ not built on.** A remote branch from the abandoned
2026-09-18 claim exists under a different name; nothing was merged, cherry-picked or
adopted from it. Its predecessor report on the card was read as information only,
and every reading reproduced here was re-taken in this worktree.
